title: CALVIN-MAX: When Does a Mid-Execution Change Hurt a Robot Policy?
abstract: arXiv:2611.31868v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Robots must often keep working after the world changes, as when a block moves or the camera shifts while the robot still acts on what it saw before. Recent work showed that one change during a task lowers success for every policy tested, but did not separate the effect of its timing from the cost of the changed world, or measure what it costs afterwards. We introduce CALVIN-MAX, a benchmark of 7,828 cases on CALVIN's five-instruction chains, each with one change to the objects, the camera, the robot, or the instruction. Each case compares three runs that are identical until the affected instruction begins: one without the change, one with it in place from that moment, and one in which it arrives while the robot is moving. The second run against the first gives the cost of the changed world, and the third against the second the effect of meeting it mid-motion. translated_title: CALVIN-MAX：执行过程中的变化何时会损害机器人策略？
translated_abstract: 机器人经常需要在世界发生变化后继续工作，例如当方块移动或相机偏移时，机器人仍基于之前看到的内容行动。近期研究表明，任务执行中的一次变化会降低所有被测试策略的成功率，但并未将变化时机的影响与世界已被改变本身的代价区分开来，也没有衡量其后产生的损失。我们提出了 CALVIN-MAX，这是一个基于 CALVIN 五指令链的基准测试，包含 7,828 个案例，每个案例对物体、相机、机器人或指令进行一次改变。每个案例比较三次运行，这三次运行在受影响指令开始之前完全相同：一次没有变化，一次变化从该时刻起就已存在，还有一次变化在机器人运动过程中到来。第二次运行与第一次运行的对比给出了世界已被改变的代价，第三次运行与第二次运行的对比则给出了在运动中途遭遇变化的影响。在每策略 1,526 个保留测试案例上，且假设预先固定，每个……（摘要至此截断）
tldr: 提出 CALVIN-MAX 基准，通过三次对照运行的设计，首次将机器人执行过程中遭遇变化的时机影响与世界已被改变的内在代价区分开来，量化了变化在运动中途到来时对策略性能的额外损害。
en_tdlr: CALVIN-MAX is a benchmark of 7,828 controlled three-run comparisons on CALVIN's five-instruction chains that disentangles the timing of mid-execution changes from the intrinsic cost of the changed world, quantifying how much more a change hurts when it arrives while the robot is moving.
